title: One Ångström at the Birth of Chemical Transmission — Claude Bernard’s 1856 Curare Frog, Langley’s 1905 Receptive Substance, Loewi’s 1921 Easter Vagusstoff & Human M2 Muscarinic / Muscle Nicotinic Locks (PDB 3UON, 4MQS, 7SMT & 9DMH)

teenKit.tldr: For decades, scientists violently argued over whether brain cells talked via electrical sparks or chemical soup, until microscopic molecular locks settled the score once and for all.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding these exact atomic locks allows modern medicine to design life-saving drugs that control heart rate, relax muscles during surgery, and target nervous system disorders with surgical precision.
keyTakeaways: Claude Bernard proved with clever frog experiments that curare poison blocks nerve signals directly at the muscle rather than freezing the brain or blood vessels.
Otto Loewi settled the bitter 'Soup vs. Sparks' debate by transferring chemical heart juice from one frog heart to another, proving neurons use chemical messengers.
High-resolution protein data banks (like PDB) reveal that neurotransmitters and toxins lock into microscopic molecular receptors with incredible sub-angström precision.

vocab.meaning: A deadly plant-derived poison used by indigenous hunters that paralyzes prey by jamming microscopic muscle receptors.
The historical name for Otto Loewi's chemical messenger (later identified as acetylcholine) that slows down the heart.
John Newport Langley's early 20th-century concept of a dedicated chemical docking site on cells before anyone had ever seen a protein.
An ultra-tiny unit of measurement equal to one ten-billionth of a meter, used by scientists to map individual atoms in biological receptors.

quiz.question: What was the core disagreement in the famous early 20th-century 'Soup vs. Sparks' scientific debate?
options: Whether neurons communicated via physical chemical squirts or direct electrical currents
Whether frog hearts could beat outside of water or required special nutrients
Whether curare poison was made from tree bark or vine extractions
Whether acetylcholine was a protein or a lipid
quiz.explanation: Scientists fiercely debated whether nerve signals leaped across synapses via electrical sparks or chemical soup.

quiz.question: How did Claude Bernard prove that curare acts specifically on muscles rather than the central nervous system?
options: By observing that curare only dissolved in cold water
By tying off a frog's blood vessel to show that poisoned blood couldn't reach the leg
By measuring the electrical resistance of the frog's brain
By watching neurons dissolve under a basic light microscope
quiz.explanation: By ligating a limb's blood supply, Bernard showed that a tied-off leg stayed alive while the rest of the body was paralyzed.

quiz.question: What did Otto Loewi do in his famous 1921 experiment to win the Nobel Prize?
options: Mapped the exact 3D atomic structure of the M2 receptor using X-rays
Fired electrical sparks directly into a human spinal cord
Transferred fluid from a stimulated frog heart to a second frog heart to make it slow down
Synthesized artificial curare in a chemistry lab
quiz.explanation: Loewi transferred chemical-laden saline solution from a stimulated frog heart to a resting one, proving chemical transmission.
